status: technical-confound association frozen before individual tag-burden values are joined to vertical-identity outcomes
role: post-freeze exploratory confound test; cannot alter v0.3.8 submission claims
question: Is individual centered vertical-identity strength systematically related to relative biologger burden (tag mass / animal mass)?

response.name: individual_null_calibrated_centered_vertical_identity
response.definition: individual observed common-cell centered identity minus that original target individual's whole-session permutation null mean
response.rationale: uses an individually null-centered identity score rather than a raw finite-sample prediction score

exposure.source: Movebank reference tables already checksum-pinned in the paper pipeline
exposure.required: both positive finite animal_mass and tag_mass for the identity-matched individual
exposure.interpretation: relative biologger load; not a direct measurement of aerodynamic drag or attachment effects

panel_test.statistic: absolute Spearman rho between relative tag burden and individual calibrated centered identity
panel_test.null: permute relative tag-burden values among matched individuals within panel; retain centered-identity values fixed

cross_panel_test.statistic: equal-panel mean absolute Spearman rho across panels with >=8 matched individuals
cross_panel_test.null: independently permute burden values within each panel and recompute equal-panel mean absolute rho
cross_panel_test.rationale: direction-free because greater relative load could either constrain movement into a more stereotyped profile or alter flight organization in the opposite direction

secondary_descriptive: matched n and tag-burden range by panel
animal-mass-only correlation reported separately but cannot replace the primary relative-burden test

interpretation_matrix.supported: A consistent monotonic association between relative tag burden and vertical-identity strength would keep tag loading as a plausible technical/biomechanical contributor, without proving causation.
interpretation_matrix.unsupported: Weakens a simple monotonic relative-tag-burden explanation of cross-panel individual vertical identity; non-monotonic or tag-specific effects remain possible.

claim_boundary: This test concerns strength of calibrated individual identity, not the direction or exact shape of vertical use.
No association cannot prove tags are irrelevant.
Association cannot distinguish payload biomechanics from correlated body-size or tag-design differences.
This extension remains outside the frozen v0.3.8 submission.
stop_rule: Do not change response source, burden definition, minimum n, absolute-rho statistic, permutation counts/seeds or support rule after the join is opened.
Do not drop a panel because its sign differs.
Do not replace relative tag burden with tag mass or body mass if the primary fails.
